cover letter

Bachelors degree or equivalent international degree and at least (5) years of professional experience OR Masters degree or equivalent international degree and at least three (3) years of professional experience. (Required)
Demonstrated ability in project management, ensuring deadlines and objectives are met, with strong organizational skills and experience creating systems accessible to diverse stakeholders.
Experience in participatory action research, community co-design frameworks, or other approaches to inclusive science generation and communication.
With generous funding and program support from the Rita Allen Foundation, the BCSP is participating in the Civic Science Fellows program for the second time.

Collaboratively plan, co-design, and execute an equity-driven civic science project embedded within BCSP mission and core pillars. Synthesize complex scientific literature and qualitative insights, establish novel engagement methodologies, and author/create high-visibility work products and/or events (e.g., reports, toolkits, media assets, workshops, symposia).

By employing a Civic Science fellow, the BCSP aims to deepen its commitment to supporting the public good by integrating sound research, harm reduction principles, and public engagement approaches. Civic Science Fellows, as a cohort nationally, are emerging leaders from diverse demographic, cultural, and professional backgrounds. They are becoming thought leaders, bridge builders, change agents, and communicators working to learn about community priorities and scientific research and bring those worlds together to create fundamentally new ways of solving problems.

Lead interdisciplinary dialogue, co-design processes, and relationship-building across academic researchers, community advocates, policymakers, and media partners directly engaged in the project. Translate project research findings into accessible, actionable insights for non-academic stakeholders.

The Civic Science Fellow will spend 18 months working on a Civic Science project within the BCSP, that draws upon evidence-based approaches connected to science communication and community engagement in order to co-create strong, diverse, and inclusive connections between science and civic life. The BCSP maintains a list of possible projects, embedded within larger Center initiatives, that it will share with the Civic Science fellow. The BCSP will engage in a collaborative process with the Civic Science fellow to determine the final project, including the problem to be addressed, the audience(s), the methodological approaches to use, the outputs created, and the engagement and dissemination strategies. The BCSP Civic Science Fellow will also have the option of proposing a co-creative new project idea within the first three months of the fellowship, aligned with the BCSP’s mission, vision, intended impact, values, and current initiatives, available on our website:

Actively participate in national Civic Science Fellows cohort learning activities, training modules, peer mentorship, cross-cohort convenings, and professional development programs supported by the Rita Allen Foundation network.
https://psychedelics.berkeley.edu/mission-vision/

Advise BCSP leadership and team members on applying national fellowship insights and project-tested civic science practices to broaden equity-driven approaches across overall Center operations and initiatives.
Familiarity with diverse methodological frameworks and fit-for-purpose research designs suited for investigating complex social issues, evaluating impact, and driving evidence-informed strategies.
Ability to independently develop, standardize, and execute novel civic engagement techniques and frameworks, contributing original procedural ideas beyond standard outreach.

Demonstrate an understanding of and/or ability to learn why the BCSP's mission is timely and relevant, as well as a nuanced appreciation of important research and social issues in contemporary psychedelic science.
Track record of delivering successful stakeholder (especially public) engagement projects, excellent project management skills, and an appreciation of the civic science approach.

Ability to review, abstract, and synthesize complex scientific literature and insights into accessible, high-impact work products (e.g., reports, policy briefs, toolkits, public scholarship, events, and workshops).
Demonstrated ability to use sound judgment, discretion, and confidentiality when responding to issues and concerns in culturally sensitive contexts.
Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite and collaborative tools that facilitate multi-stakeholder engagement.
